A plank of non-uniform density which has a mass of $15 \text{ kg}$ is used to make a see-saw. A pivot is placed under the centre of the plank as shown on the diagram.
A boy of mass $35 \text{ kg}$ sits at one end of the plank with his centre of gravity $1.20 \text{ m}$ from the pivot. The see-saw balances when a woman of mass $60 \text{ kg}$ sits on the plank on the other side of the pivot. Her centre of gravity is $0.80 \text{ m}$ from the pivot.
Where is the centre of gravity of the plank and what is the magnitude of the force between the pivot and the plank?
(The gravitational field strength $g$ is $10 \text{ N kg}^{-1}.)$

|  | distance from pivot | force / N |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | $0.40 \text{ m}$ on left of pivot | 100 |
| B | $0.40 \text{ m}$ on left of pivot | 1100 |
| C | at the pivot | 100 |
| D | at the pivot | 1100 |
| E | $0.20 \text{ m}$ on right of pivot | 100 |
| F | $0.20 \text{ m}$ on right of pivot | 1100 |
| G | $0.40 \text{ m}$ on right of pivot | 100 |
| H | $0.40 \text{ m}$ on right of pivot | 1100 |
